hr_cap.reason: Until the Week 1 time trial; then ~85% of threshold HR.
85% of threshold HR 177 from the 15 Oct time trial.

bagels_run.note: The run club's Tuesday-morning run. Kept by choice; moderate HR is expected.

four_lap.pace_rule: Set at Checkpoint B: 4:15 if a checkpoint fails; 4:05 only if B passes with room to spare.

osaka.note: First marathon, run with a friend. Finishing together is the goal, not the time. Don't start ahead of your block.

phases.name: Build the engine
phases.note: More easy kilometres; quality reps get longer before they get faster.

phases.name: Four laps at pace
phases.note: Full 4-lap reps; rest stretches to test conditions.

phases.name: Osaka
phases.note: The marathon is the only goal. Long run to 30 km, then three weeks of taper.

notes: Time trial on the field, on fresh legs. Count the laps: laps x ~465 m gives threshold pace.
Average HR over the last 20 minutes is threshold HR. The easy cap becomes ~85% of it; until then, keep 155.
Two laps you can already hold. The point is six even reps, not one fast one.
The third lap is the wall right now. Slower pace on purpose, to practise running through it.
First time at 4:10 over the full 4 laps. Rest is longer so the pace is honest.
Test conditions from here: full 10-minute rest.
Last hard session before the test. Stop while it still feels good.
The long run stays at 14 km, easy: the marathon still needs it.
Rep one should feel almost too easy. Every rep within 5 s of the last.
Easy runs before the test are very easy. The day after it is rest or a 20-minute walk.
The long run starts the marathon block.
The test replaces the Bagels Run this week.
Christmas week. If a run goes, cut easy kilometres, never the long run.
Start practising fuel on long runs over 90 minutes: a gel or chews every 35-40 min.
January heat: long runs start at first light. Hold the HR cap and let pace drift.
Volume drops on purpose. Don't top it up.
Run long runs with your race friend where you can, at their race pace.
Wear race shoes and race kit on the long run.
Long run: 30 km or 3 h 30, whichever comes first. Full race-day fuel and breakfast rehearsal.
Longest run of the block. Nothing after this makes you fitter for Osaka; it only has to not make you tired.
Quality: inside an easy 6 km, early in the week, at race pace.
Other runs: a very easy 2.5 km early in the week and a 20-minute shake-out in Osaka. Travel days count as rest.
The day before: rest, bib pick-up, carb-heavy dinner, early night.
The first 10 km should feel too slow. If you both feel good at 30 km, that's when 4:30 decides itself.

A.pass: All three reps at 4:15-4:25 and the last no slower than the first -> advance to Week 5.
A.fail: Otherwise -> repeat Week 3's targets next week instead of advancing; the December target moves to 4:15.

B.pass: All four within 5 s and controlled -> test at 4:10. Last rep the fastest and still in control -> may try 4:05.
B.fail: Can't hold 4:10 for four reps -> test at 4:15. 4:00 is back only if this session feels easy.

weekly-shape.title: Weekly shape
lines: One quality session and one long run per week, never on consecutive days (a Sunday long run then a Monday quality session counts).
Until 15 Dec the quality session builds to the 4-lap test; a tempo or a social run doesn't replace it.
Everything else is easy, under the HR cap, judged by HR rather than pace, except the Bagels Run. Any day works.
The quality session is never the day after the Bagels Run.
If something has to give, cut easy kilometres first and the long run last.

laps.title: Laps, not kilometres
lines: A lap is roughly 450-480 m, so 4 laps is about 1.8-1.9 km. The goal is 4 laps, whatever they measure.
Run to the average pace on your watch and count laps.

quality-session.title: Every quality session
lines: 12-15 minutes easy, then 4 x 20 s strides, then the work. Ten minutes easy after.
Hold the target pace on every rep. If you want a max effort, make it the last rep.
Threshold is the pace from the Week 1 time trial. Test pace is the pace set at Checkpoint B.

easy-means-easy.title: Easy means easy
lines: Easy runs and long runs stay under the HR cap, whatever pace that takes.
Until 16 Dec the long-run distance is the plan's number, not a minimum. Extra moderate kilometres get paid for at the next quality session.

strength.title: Strength, 20 minutes
lines: As many times as the week says, on any days; best straight after the quality session or an easy run.
Three rounds, 60 s between rounds: squats x 15, split squats x 10 each leg, single-leg calf raises x 15 each side, single-leg glute bridge x 12 each side, pogo hops x 20.
Skip the circuit if you're sore enough that your squat depth suffers.

marathon-long-runs.title: Marathon long runs
lines: 7:00-7:15/km, ideally with your race friend. Their pace is the race pace.
Over 90 minutes: fuel every 35-40 minutes with what you'll use in Osaka.
January heat: start at first light, keep the HR cap, let pace slow.
Osaka will be cold at the 9:15 start. Rehearse race kit on the 28 and 30 km runs.

bad-session.title: If a session goes badly
lines: One bad session is information. Cut it short, note what happened, carry on.
Three in a row means volume is climbing faster than you're absorbing it: repeat the previous week's targets instead of advancing.
